query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

decision.trend: Research has been focused on improving the strength and ductility of high-entropy alloys through various processing techniques and microstructural design. Earlier studies have shown that conventional processing methods can raise strength at the expense of ductility, while recent studies have explored alternative methods such as thermal or thermomechanical treatment, and microstructure architecture design. The trend suggests that a combination of these approaches may be necessary to achieve both high strength and ductility.
decision.unsolved: Despite the progress made, room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility remain significant challenges for high-entropy alloys. The development of a single intervention that can improve both strength and ductility remains an open question.
decision.why: The recent study (PMC10213035) demonstrated the potential of stepwise thermo-mechanical processes in generating ultrahigh strength and ductile refractory high-entropy alloys. Building on this work, the next step could involve exploring the application of similar processes to other high-entropy alloy systems, with a focus on optimizing the treatment parameters to achieve a balance between strength and ductility.
